Teide National Park, also known as Parque Nacional del Teide, is a beautiful national park located on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands, Spain. Specifically, it's situated in the center and northwest regions of the island.

The park surrounds Mount Teide (Pico del Teide), the highest peak in Spain (3,718 meters above sea level) and also one of the highest volcanoes in the world. The park was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Centre in 2007 and is also part of the Canary Islands' special reserve.

Islands like Tenerife are geographically unique due to their location near North Africa but within the subtropical latitudes of Europe, which often creates dramatic natural landscapes with diverse volcanic features. Teide National Park showcases these unique geological properties, making it a popular destination for nature lovers and tourists interested in exploring volcanic terrain. Visiting this park allows visitors from around the world an opportunity to experience unique ecosystems that thrive under challenging conditions created by the island's volcanic activity.

Teide National Park offers stunning landscapes, diverse wildlife (including birds), and a significant cultural and environmental importance due to its geological features. Its accessibility and attractions make it a notable destination within the Canary Islands' tourism offerings.
Garajonay National Park is located on the island of La Gomera, which is one of the Canary Islands, Spain. It was actually designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986 for its unique laurisilva forest ecosystem that has been preserved since the Tertiary period (over 20 million years ago).
